first.rationale: A guarded onboarding simplification test directly addresses the observed completion decline and is supported by prior self-serve adoption evidence. Promotional pricing is the most consequential alternative given competitor pressure, so its archived evidence should be checked before rejecting it; pricing may create acquisition lift at the expense of sustainable unit economics or account quality. Simplification should be monitored for downstream qualification and retention, not only completion.

final.rationale: Run a standard, controlled onboarding-shortening experiment for self-serve accounts. This directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and uses verified evidence of +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified short-term qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failed the sustainable-growth objective. Evaluate completion and activation alongside qualified conversion, retention, and early expansion signals before rollout.
